network.overall_strategy: Build the threonine carbon skeleton by converging on 2-amino-3-hydroxybutanenitrile. Eight pathways arise from combining two routes to glycine nitrile (stepwise methanimine trapping or one-pot Strecker), two routes to acetaldehyde (hydrothermal pyruvate decarboxylation or UV-driven ethanol dehydrogenation), and two endgame hydrolysis regimes (overall nitrile hydrolysis or stepwise hydrolysis via threonine amide). Two additional pathways come from hydroxyacetone isomerization to lactaldehyde followed by Strecker chemistry and the same two hydrolysis regimes. The network is nonenzymatic and therefore targets the threonine constitutional isomer rather than a single stereoisomer; racemic and diastereomeric threonine/allothreonine mixtures are expected.

reactions.name: Condensation of formaldehyde and ammonia to methanimine

conditions.other: evaporating surface films or wet-dry cycling; neutral to mildly alkaline; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds to formaldehyde to form a carbinolamine, which dehydrates during dry-down to methanimine.
reactions.reasoning: Formaldehyde is highly electrophilic and reacts readily with ammonia; in drying surface films the carbinolamine dehydrates to methanimine. This is the standard imine entry point for Strecker-type aminonitrile synthesis.

reactions.name: Cyanide capture of methanimine to give glycine nitrile

conditions.other: HCN-bearing shallow pool or thin film; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide attacks the iminium form of methanimine, yielding the aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Addition of cyanide to a small imine is the key C-C bond-forming step of the Strecker reaction. Rapid trapping of transient methanimine makes glycine nitrile a credible prebiotic hub.

reactions.name: One-pot Strecker synthesis of glycine nitrile

conditions.other: one-pot evaporitic brine or tidal-flat pool; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: In situ methanimine formation is followed immediately by cyanide capture, giving glycine nitrile without isolating the imine.
reactions.reasoning: When formaldehyde, ammonia, and HCN coexist, aminonitrile formation can occur in one pot. This operationally distinct route avoids the need for a separately accumulating methanimine pool.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetaldehyde

conditions.other: subseafloor hydrothermal mixing zone; anoxic; rapid quench helps preserve acetaldehyde

reactions.mechanism: Thermal and mineral-assisted decarboxylation of the alpha-keto acid releases CO2 and furnishes acetaldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: Alpha-keto acids are thermally labile, and hydrothermal temperatures plus iron-rich mineral surfaces favor decarboxylation to simpler aldehydes. Pyruvate therefore provides an anoxic vent-compatible, though transient, source of acetaldehyde.

reactions.name: UV-driven dehydrogenation of ethanol to acetaldehyde

conditions.other: UV-irradiated shallow film in a subaerial geothermal field; anoxic; short irradiation limits overoxidation

reactions.mechanism: UV-excited semiconductor holes oxidize ethanol to acetaldehyde while electrons are discharged by proton reduction.
reactions.reasoning: Strong early-Earth UV and semiconducting oxides can drive alcohol dehydrogenation without molecular oxygen. TiO2-bearing grains provide a plausible second source of acetaldehyde, although overoxidation is a competing side process.

reactions.name: Aldol-type homologation of glycine nitrile with acetaldehyde

conditions.other: concentrated prebiotic pool at a mineral interface; mildly alkaline; low water activity; threonine/allothreonine nitrile mixture expected

reactions.mechanism: Deprotonation alpha to the nitrile generates a nucleophilic aminonitrile/enamine equivalent that adds to acetaldehyde; protonation gives the beta-hydroxy aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This C-C bond-forming step is more speculative than classical Strecker chemistry, but glycine nitrile has an acidified alpha-C-H next to the nitrile and can plausibly undergo mineral-assisted addition to aldehydes. In concentrated alkaline films this provides a compact route to the threonine carbon skeleton and is a likely network bottleneck.

reactions.name: Mineral-catalyzed isomerization of hydroxyacetone to lactaldehyde

conditions.other: mildly alkaline hot-spring or evaporitic pool

reactions.mechanism: Enediol-mediated keto-aldehyde isomerization shifts the carbonyl position from C2 to C1.
reactions.reasoning: Hydroxyacetone and lactaldehyde are carbonyl isomers connected by enediol chemistry. Borate-bearing mineral settings can facilitate such isomerizations and transiently stabilize hydroxycarbonyls, although selectivity in complex mixtures is uncertain.

reactions.name: Strecker synthesis of threonine nitrile from lactaldehyde

conditions.other: HCN/NH3-rich pool; threonine/allothreonine nitrile mixture expected

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia forms an imine with lactaldehyde, then cyanide adds to the iminium carbon to give the aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Once lactaldehyde is available, classical Strecker chemistry yields the correct threonine skeleton in one step. Because the precursor is already alpha-hydroxylated, the reaction naturally furnishes beta-hydroxy alpha-aminonitriles.

reactions.name: Overall hydrolysis of threonine nitrile to threonine

conditions.other: prolonged geothermal cycling or long residence times in prebiotic pools

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration and amide hydrolysis occur under extended aqueous heating; the amide does not accumulate as a discrete pool.
reactions.reasoning: Aminonitriles are more hydrolytically robust than amino acids but can convert to the corresponding amino acid during prolonged heating in water. This lumped step represents conditions where overall nitrile-to-acid hydrolysis proceeds without a persistent threonine amide intermediate.

reactions.name: Partial hydrolysis of threonine nitrile to threonine amide

conditions.other: shorter or milder hydrolysis regime in a prebiotic pool

reactions.mechanism: Water adds to the nitrile under heating to produce the corresponding primary amide.
reactions.reasoning: Under milder or shorter hydrolysis regimes, nitriles often stop at the amide stage. Threonine amide is therefore a plausible accumulating late intermediate.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of threonine amide to threonine
reactions.mechanism: Aqueous amide hydrolysis converts the amide carbonyl to the carboxylic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Amide hydrolysis is slower than nitrile hydration and is a likely late-stage bottleneck. Repeated geothermal cycling can nevertheless drive threonine amide to threonine over longer timescales.

pathways.name: Stepwise glycine nitrile route with hydrothermal acetaldehyde and direct hydrolysis
pathways.description: Methanimine is formed by dry condensation, trapped by HCN to give glycine nitrile, converged with hydrothermal acetaldehyde from pyruvate, then hydrolyzed directly from threonine nitrile to threonine.

pathways.name: Stepwise glycine nitrile route with photochemical acetaldehyde and direct hydrolysis
pathways.description: Methanimine-derived glycine nitrile is combined with acetaldehyde generated by UV-driven ethanol dehydrogenation, followed by direct hydrolysis of threonine nitrile.

pathways.name: One-pot glycine nitrile route with hydrothermal acetaldehyde and direct hydrolysis
pathways.description: A one-pot Strecker reaction forms glycine nitrile, which is homologated with vent-derived acetaldehyde and then hydrolyzed directly to threonine.

pathways.name: One-pot glycine nitrile route with photochemical acetaldehyde and direct hydrolysis
pathways.description: One-pot Strecker formation of glycine nitrile converges with UV-generated acetaldehyde from ethanol, then proceeds through direct hydrolysis of threonine nitrile.

pathways.name: Stepwise glycine nitrile route with hydrothermal acetaldehyde via threonine amide
pathways.description: The methanimine-mediated glycine nitrile branch meets hydrothermal acetaldehyde and then proceeds through threonine amide before reaching threonine.

pathways.name: Stepwise glycine nitrile route with photochemical acetaldehyde via threonine amide
pathways.description: The methanimine-mediated glycine nitrile branch meets UV-generated acetaldehyde and reaches threonine through a persistent threonine amide stage.

pathways.name: One-pot glycine nitrile route with hydrothermal acetaldehyde via threonine amide
pathways.description: One-pot glycine nitrile formation is followed by homologation with hydrothermal acetaldehyde and a stepwise hydrolysis sequence through threonine amide.

pathways.name: One-pot glycine nitrile route with photochemical acetaldehyde via threonine amide
pathways.description: One-pot glycine nitrile formation converges with photochemically generated acetaldehyde and proceeds through threonine amide to the target.

pathways.name: Hydroxyacetone-lactaldehyde Strecker route with direct hydrolysis
pathways.description: Hydroxyacetone isomerizes to lactaldehyde, which undergoes classical Strecker chemistry to threonine nitrile followed by direct hydrolysis to threonine.

pathways.name: Hydroxyacetone-lactaldehyde Strecker route via threonine amide
pathways.description: Hydroxyacetone enters through lactaldehyde and Strecker chemistry, but the endgame proceeds stepwise through threonine amide.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is connected, uses molecule IDs consistently, and offers a chemically sensible set of alternative routes to the threonine carbon skeleton, with the lactaldehyde Strecker branch being the strongest overall. The main validity problem is stoichiometric: 7 of 11 reactions are unbalanced by the supplied deterministic check, specifically rxn_001 needs H2O, rxn_003 needs H2O, rxn_004 needs CO2, rxn_005 needs H2 or an explicit oxidant or electron sink, rxn_008 needs H2O, rxn_009 should be written overall as mol_011 + 2 mol_014 -> mol_013 + mol_002, and rxn_011 should be mol_012 + mol_014 -> mol_013 + mol_002; adding CO2 and H2 also requires new molecule nodes. Chemically, rxn_006 is the least secure transformation and needs stronger mechanistic or literature support, while the hydrolysis and homologation steps are weakened by being assigned to a Biochemical environment despite the stated nonenzymatic framework. The target is nominally reached, likely as a threonine/allothreonine mixture, but the current network is not approvable until the conservation errors are corrected and the key nonenzymatic conditions are specified more rigorously.
